paper.title: Minimax and Bayes Optimal Adaptive Experimental Design for Treatment Choice

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive experiment for treatment choice (binary treatments, fixed budget, worst-case simple regret)
unmapped: Each arm's outcome follows a mean-parameterized canonical exponential family with arm-specific variance function sigma_d^2(mu), sub-Gaussian, mean in a compact interval M; families may differ across arms
settings.definition_quote: Given binary treatments, the experimenter's goal is to choose the treatment with the highest expected outcome through an adaptive experiment ... Regret^delta_mu := E_mu[Y_{d*} - Y_{\hat d_T}] = E_mu[mu_{d*} - mu_{\hat d_T}] ... Worst-case regret: sup_{mu in M^2} Regret^delta_mu.

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive experiment for treatment choice (minimax lower bound)
unmapped: Each arm's outcome follows a mean-parameterized canonical exponential family with known variance function sigma_d^2(mu), sub-Gaussian, mean in compact interval M
settings.definition_quote: Fix an outcome space $\calY$, a parameter space $\calM \subset \bbR$, and a set of variance functions $\bm{\sigma}^2 = (\sigma^2_d)_{d \in \{1, 0\}}$ with $\sigma^2 \colon \{1, 0\} \times \calM \to (0, \infty)$. Suppose that the marginal distribution of each $Y_{d, t}$ is $P_{d, \mu_d}$ such that $\bmP_{\bmmu} = (P_{d, \mu_d})_{d\in\{1, 0\}} \in \calB_{\bm{\sigma}^2}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive experiment for treatment choice (average/Bayes regret, upper bound)
unmapped: Mean-parameterized canonical exponential family outcomes with arm-specific variance functions; variances unknown

settings.name_in_paper: Adaptive experiment for treatment choice (Bayes lower bound)
unmapped: Mean-parameterized canonical exponential family outcomes with known variance functions
settings.definition_quote: Let H be a prior distribution on M^2 ... for any prior H satisfying Assumption 5.1

symbols.sigma_bar_1: sup over mu in M of sigma_1(mu) (worst-case std of treatment 1)
symbols.sigma_bar_0: sup over mu in M of sigma_0(mu)

conditions: Outcomes in mean-parameterized canonical exponential family B_{sigma^2} with compact mean space M
for all experiments in A (all allocation rules and recommendation rules)

source.label: thm:minimax_lowerbound
source.quote: Then the following lower bound holds: \inf_{\delta \in \calA} \liminf_{T \to \infty} \sqrt{T} \sup_{\bmmu \in \calM^2} \text{Regret}^\delta_{\bmmu} \geq \Bigp{\overline{\sigma}_1 + \overline{\sigma}_0} \Phi(-1), where \overline{\sigma}^2_d \coloneqq \sup_{\mu\in\calM} \sigma^2_d(\mu).

results.notes: Bound on sqrt(T)*worst-case simple regret; expression divided by sqrt(T). Regret is expected simple regret defined through means. Proof's final step is loose (sup over mu with arm-specific sup).

symbols.sigma_bar_1: sup over mu in M of sigma_1(mu)
symbols.sigma_bar_0: sup over mu in M of sigma_0(mu)

conditions: Outcomes in mean-parameterized canonical exponential family B_{sigma^2} (sub-Gaussian) with compact mean space M
tuning: split ratio r in (0,1) with r/2 <= min_d sigma_bar_d / (sigma_bar_1 + sigma_bar_0)

source.label: thm:minimax_upperbound
source.quote: If $r / 2 \leq \min_{d\in\{1, 0\}}\overline{\sigma}_d \big/ \sum_{b \in \{1, 0\}} \overline{\sigma}_b$, then the regret of the TSNA experiment satisfies \limsup_{T \to \infty} \sup_{\bmmu \in \calM^2} \sqrt{T} \text{Regret}^{\delta^{\text{TSNA}}}_{\bmmu} \leq \Bigp{\overline{\sigma}_1 + \overline{\sigma}_0}\Phi(-1).

results.notes: Combined with Theorem 5.1 in Corollary 6.2 (asymptotic minimax optimality). Condition on r requires knowing a bound on worst-case std ratio.

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{\delta} \liminf_{T\to\infty} T \int \text{Regret}^{\delta}_{\bmmu} dH(\bmmu) \geq \frac{1}{4}\sum_{d}\int_{\mu} h_d(\mu \mid \mu_{\backslash d})(\sigma_1(\mu) + \sigma_0(\mu))^2 dH_{\backslash d}(\mu)

symbols.B_H: (1/4) * sum_{d in {1,0}} int_M h_d(mu | mu_{\d}) (sigma_1(mu) + sigma_0(mu))^2 dH_{\d}(mu), prior-dependent constant

conditions: prior H has uniformly continuous conditional densities (Assumption 5.1)
Outcomes in mean-parameterized canonical exponential family B_{sigma^2}

source.label: thm:bayes_lowerbound
source.quote: Then, for any prior $H$ satisfying Assumption~\ref{asm:uniformcontinuity}, the following lower bound holds: \inf_{\delta \in \calA} \liminf_{T \to \infty} T \int_{\bmmu \in \calM^2} \text{Regret}^{\delta}_{\bmmu} \rmd H(\bmmu) \geq \frac{1}{4}\sum_{d\in\{1, 0\}}\int_{\mu \in \calM}h_d(\mu \mid \mu_{\backslash d})\bigp{\sigma_1(\mu) + \sigma_0(\mu)}^2\rmd H_{\backslash d}(\mu)

results.notes: Average (Bayes) simple regret over prior H scaled by T; expression divided by T. Dependence field set to worst_case as it is not instance-specific (prior-averaged).

bound.expression_latex: \limsup_{T \to \infty} T\int \text{Regret}^{\delta^{\text{TSNA}}}_{\bmmu} dH(\bmmu) \leq \frac{1}{4}\sum_{d}\int_{\mu} h_d(\mu \mid \mu_{\backslash d})(\sigma_1(\mu) + \sigma_0(\mu))^2 dH_{\backslash d}(\mu)

symbols.B_H: (1/4) * sum_{d in {1,0}} int_M h_d(mu | mu_{\d}) (sigma_1(mu) + sigma_0(mu))^2 dH_{\d}(mu), prior-dependent constant

conditions: Outcomes in mean-parameterized canonical exponential family B_{sigma^2}
prior H with conditional densities h_d (as in Assumption 5.1)
tuning: r/2 <= sigma_d(mu)/(sigma_d(mu)+sigma_b(mu)) for all mu in M

source.label: thm:bayes_upperbound
source.quote: Also suppose that $r / 2 \leq \min_{a\neq b}\sigma_d(\mu) \big/ \bigp{\sigma_d(\mu) + \sigma_b(\mu)}$ holds for all $\mu\in\calM$. Then, the TSNA experiment satisfies the following average upper bound: \limsup_{T \to \infty} T\int_{\bmmu \in \calM^2} \text{Regret}^{\delta^{\text{TSNA}}}_{\bmmu}\rmd H(\bmmu) \leq \frac{1}{4}\sum_{d}\int h_d(\mu \mid \mu_{\backslash d})(\sigma_1(\mu) + \sigma_0(\mu))^2 dH_{\backslash d}(\mu).

results.notes: Corollary 6.4 combines with Theorem 5.2 (stated 'as r -> 0') for asymptotic Bayes optimality. Algorithm does not use the prior.

symbols.v: max over arms of the sub-Gaussian variance proxy of the outcomes

conditions: outcomes sub-Gaussian with variance proxy v_d
same conditions as Proposition 6.5 (allocation ratio converges a.s. to w in (0,1))

source.label: lem:upper_probabilityofmisidentiifcation
source.quote: Then, for $v \coloneqq \max_{d \in \{1, 0\}} v_d$, it holds that \bbP_{\bmmu}\Bigp{\widehat{\mu}_{d^*_{\bmmu}, T} < \widehat{\mu}_{\widehat{d}^{\delta^{\text{TSNA}}}, T}} \leq 2\exp\p{-\frac{rT \Delta^2_{\bmmu}}{16 v}}.

results.notes: Misidentification probability of TSNA; auxiliary lemma used in upper-bound proofs. Delta = |mu_1 - mu_0|.
